zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Sabaʾ
﷽
﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ ولَهُ الحَمْدُ في الآخِرَةِ﴾: Allah is the One praised in this world and the Hereafter. His being praised in the Hereafter is indicated by the words of the people of Paradise: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنا وعْدَهُ وأوْرَثَنا الأرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشاءُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 74], that is: He has made us inherit the land of Paradise.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ في الأرْضِ وما يَخْرُجُ مِنها﴾, that is: what enters the earth and what comes out of it — what enters the earth of rain and other things, and what comes out of it of crops and other things. ﴿وَما يَنْـزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وما يَعْرُجُ فِيها﴾: what ascends in it. One says: ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرُجُ“ when one ascends, and ”اَلْمَعارِجُ“ are the steps, from this. One also says: ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرِجُ“ when one becomes lame (dhā ʿaraj), and ”عَرَجَ، يَعْرُجُ“ when one limps from something that has befallen him. «[Translator's note: the source prints the ascending verb as ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرُجُ“; the usual form is ʿaraja, yaʿruju; it is translated as written.]»

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَأْتِينا السّاعَةُ﴾: the Hour in which creation is resurrected. The meaning is that they said: "We will not be resurrected." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ بَلى ورَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكم عالِمِ الغَيْبِ لا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ مِثْقالُ ذَرَّةٍ﴾, with the genitive in ”عالِمِ“, as an attribute (ṣifa) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is also read in the nominative, on two accounts. One of them is as mubtadaʾ (subject), the meaning being: "The Knower of the unseen — nothing escapes Him", so that ”لا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”عالِمُ الغَيْبِ“. And it is made nominative by way of praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the meaning being: "He is the Knower of the unseen". The accusative is also permissible, though it has not been read, on the meaning: "Remember the Knower of the unseen". It is also read: ”عَلّامُ الغُيُوبِ“, and ”عَلّامَ الغَيْبِ“ is permissible. It is also read: ”لا يَعْزِبُ عَنْهُ“ with kasra on the zāy. One says: ”عَزَبَ عَنِّي، يَعْزُبُ، ويَعْزِبُ“ when something is hidden [from one].

zajjaj:4-4.t:
﴿لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: the lām has come in as a response to His words: ﴿قُلْ بَلى ورَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 3], for recompense, that is: for the sake of recompense with reward and punishment.
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ ورِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: Allah has made clear that their recompense is forgiveness, which is the covering over of sins.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His words, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿والَّذِينَ سَعَوْا في آياتِنا مُعاجِزِينَ﴾: it is also read: ”مُعَجِّزِينَ“. ”مُعاجِزِينَ“ is in the sense of ”مُسابِقِينَ“ (racing to outdo). Whoever reads ”مُعَجِّزِينَ“, its meaning is that they hinder (yuʿajjizūna) those who believe in them, so it is in the sense of ”مُثَبِّطِينَ“ (holding back), and that is the meaning of their hindering those who believe in them.
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم عَذابٌ مِن رِجْزٍ ألِيمٌ﴾: ”ألِيمٍ“ in the genitive is a naʿt (adjective) of al-zajz «[Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for al-rijz (”رِجْزٍ“)]», and ”ألِيمٌ“ [in the nominative] is a naʿt of al-ʿadhāb.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَيَرى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ هو الحَقَّ﴾: here [those given knowledge are] the scholars of the Jews who believed in the Prophet — upon him be peace —, among them Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. That is: ”وَلِيَرى“ (and so that … may see); the position of ”يَرى“ is conjoined to His words: ”لِيَجْزِيَ“. ”اَلْحَقَّ“ is accusative, a khabar (predicate) of ”يَرى الَّذِينَ“ «[Translator's note: i.e. the second object of yarā]». ”هو“ here is a faṣl (separating pronoun) indicating that what follows it is not a naʿt (adjective); the Kufans call it al-ʿimād (the support). ”هو“ does not enter as an ʿimād except with a definite noun and what resembles it; we have explained that in what has gone before. The nominative is permissible in His words ”هو الحَقُّ“.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكم عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾, the verse: this is the saying of the idolaters who do not believe in the resurrection; some of them say to others: "Shall we point you to Muḥammad, who claims that you will be resurrected after you have become bones, dust and crumbled remains?" In this verse there is a subtle point of Arabic, and we shall explain it, if Allah wills. ”إذا“ is in the position of the accusative through ”مُزِّقْتُمْ“, and ”جَدِيدٍ“ cannot govern it, because what comes after ”أنْ“ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is إنَّ]» does not govern what precedes it. The interpretation is: "Shall we point you to a man who says to you that, when you are torn to pieces, you will be resurrected?" So ”إذا“ is in the position of the ”إنْ“ of condition (al-jazāʾ), governed by what follows it. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said:
إذا قَصُرَتْ أسْيافُنا كانَ وصْلُها ∗∗∗ خُطانا إلى أعْدائِنا فَنُضارِبْ
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we strike.)
The meaning is: "their extension will be"; the proof of that is the jussive of ”فَنُضارِبْ“. It may also be that what governs ”إذا“ is an implied (muḍmar) [verb], indicated by ”إنَّكم لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, the meaning being: "Shall we point you to a man who informs you, saying to you: when you are torn to pieces you will be resurrected — you will be in a new creation?", just as they said: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا وعِظامًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 16], where ”إذا“ may be accusative through a verb indicated by ”إنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ“. ”أنَّكم لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“ with fatḥa is not permissible, because when the lām comes, nothing but kasra of ”إنَّ“ is permissible.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وما خَلْفَهم مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: "Have they not reflected and known that the One who created the heaven and the earth is able to resurrect them, and able to make the earth swallow them, or to make the heaven fall upon them in fragments?"
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾, that is: in that there is a sign that shows whoever turns to Allah, returns to Him and reflects on what He has created, that He is able to give life to the dead.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنّا فَضْلا يا جِبالُ أوِّبِي مَعَهُ والطَّيْرَ﴾: the meaning is: “And We said: O mountains, repeat [praise] with him. It is also read: “ أُوبِي مَعَهُ ”, on the meaning “ return to glorification with him whenever he returns to it ”. Whoever reads: “ أوِّبِي مَعَهُ ”, its meaning is: echo with him; one says: “ آبَ، يَؤُوبُ ” when one returns. The meaning of “ رَجِّعِي مَعَهُ ” is: glorify with him, and echo the glorification with him. “ والطَّيْرَ ” and “ والطَّيْرُ ”: the nominative is on two accounts. One of them is that it be conjoined (nasaq) to what is in “ أوِّبِي ” [i.e. its pronoun]; the meaning is: “ O mountains, echo the glorification, you and the birds ”. It may also be nominative as a badal (substitute); the meaning is: “ O mountains, and O birds, echo with him ”. The accusative is on three accounts: that it be conjoined to His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنّا فَضْلا﴾ ﴿والطَّيْرَ﴾, that is: and We subjected the birds to him — Abū ʿUbayda related that from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ. It may be accusative by the vocative (al-nidāʾ); the meaning is: “ O mountains, echo with him, and the birds ”, as though He said: “ We called the mountains and the birds ”, so “ اَلطَّيْرَ ” is conjoined to the position of “ اَلْجِبالَ ” in origin; every one addressed (munādā) — according to all the Basrans — is in the position of the accusative. We have explained the state of the vocative with ḍamma, and that the definite one is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma. And it may be that “ والطَّيْرَ ” is accusative on the meaning of “ مَعَ ” (with), as you say: “ قُمْتُ وزَيْدًا ”, that is: “ I stood with Zayd ”; so the meaning is: “ echo with him and with the birds ".

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 10] ﴿أنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ﴾, that is: We made it soft. The first to make coats of mail was David; before that, the iron with which people protected themselves was only pieces of iron, like these breastplates (al-jawāshin).
”أنْ“ here is in the sense of explanation (al-tafsīr), as though it were said: ”وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ أيِ اعْمَلَ سابِغاتٍ“ (and We softened iron for him, that is: make full coats of mail), in the sense of "We said to him: make full coats of mail". It may also be in the sense of: "so that he might make full coats of mail", with ”أنْ“ joined to the wording of the imperative. Like this in speech is ”أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِ أنْ قُمْ إلَيَّ“ (he sent to him: stand and come to me), that is: he said: "Go to so-and-so"; and it may be in the sense of: "send to him that he should go to so-and-so". The meaning of ”سابِغاتٍ“ is: ample coats of mail; He mentioned the attribute because it indicates what is qualified. The meaning of ”اَلسّابِغُ“ is that which covers everything it is on, so that it is more than enough. ﴿وَقَدِّرْ في السَّرْدِ﴾: ”اَلسَّرْدُ“ in the language is bringing one thing up to another so that you produce it in order, one part following another in succession; from it is ”سَرَدَ فُلانٌ الحَدِيثَ“ (so-and-so narrated the account in sequence). It is said in the exegesis: ”اَلسَّرْدُ“ is riveting, covering and forming the rings. It is also said: it is that he should not make the rivet thick and the hole narrow, nor make the rivet thin and the hole wide, so that it rattles, comes loose and breaks. ”قَدِّرْ في ذَلِكَ“, that is: make it in due proportion and according to need. What has come in the exegesis does not depart from the language, because riveting is your bringing one end of the ring up to its other end. Sībawayh claimed that the saying of the Arabs ”رَجُلٌ سَرَنْدِيٌّ“ is derived from ”اَلسَّرْدُ“, because its meaning is "the bold one"; he said: "the bold one" is he who goes straight ahead.
The explanation of ﴿وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 10] is: We made it soft like threads, yielding to him, so that he made the coats of mail.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ﴾: the accusative in ”اَلرِّيحَ“ is the [preferred] way, and it is the reading of most readers, on the meaning: "and We subjected the wind to Solomon". The nominative is also permissible: ”وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحُ غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ“, the nominative being on the meaning: "the wind was established for him", and in meaning it comes back to the sense of "We subjected the wind", just as when you say: ”لِلَّهِ الحَمْدُ“, its interpretation is: "praise is established for Allah", and it comes back to the meaning: "I praise Allah with praise".
His words: ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ ورَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾, that is: its morning course is a month's journey, and likewise its evening course. Solomon would sit on his throne together with his companions, and the wind would carry them in the morning a month's journey and carry them in the evening a month's journey. ﴿وَأسَلْنا لَهُ عَيْنَ القِطْرِ﴾: ”اَلْقِطْرُ“ is copper, which is brass (al-ṣufr); it was melted from that time on, and before Solomon it did not melt. ﴿وَمِنَ الجِنِّ مَن يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is accusative; the meaning is: "We subjected to him, of the jinn, those who work". The position of ”مَن“ may also be nominative, the meaning being: "among what We gave him, of the jinn, are those who work before him by the permission of his Lord", that is: by the command of his Lord. ﴿وَمَن يَزِغْ مِنهم عَنْ أمْرِنا﴾, that is: "whoever deviates".

zajjaj:13-13.t:
Then He made clear what they used to do before him, saying: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِن مَحارِيبَ وتَماثِيلَ﴾: ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“ is that in which one prays, and the most honoured place in a dwelling and in a house is called ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“. ﴿وَجِفانٍ كالجَوابِ﴾: most readers pause without a yāʾ. The original was to pause with the yāʾ, except that the kasra stands in for it. Without the alif and lām, the pause on it is without a yāʾ — you say: ”هَذِهِ جَوابٍ“ — and then the alif and lām were added, and the word was left as it was before they were added. ”اَلْجَوابِي“ is the plural of ”جابِيَةٌ“, and ”اَلْجابِيَةُ“ is the large basin. Al-Aʿshā said:
كَجابِيَةِ السِّيجِ العِراقِيِّ تَفْهَقُ
(Like the basin of the Iraqi [estate-]wall, brimming over.)
That is: they make for him his bowls like the great basins in which water is collected. ﴿وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: fixed. ﴿اعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْرًا﴾: ”شُكْرًا“ is accusative on two accounts. One of them: work for [the sake of] thanks, that is: thank Allah for what He has given you. And ”اِعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْرًا“ may be on the meaning: give thanks with thanks.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿ما دَلَّهم عَلى مَوْتِهِ إلا دابَّةُ الأرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأتَهُ﴾: ”اَلْمِنسَأةُ“ is the staff. It was only called ”مِنسَأةً“ because one drives with it (yunsaʾu bihā), and the meaning of ”يُنْسَأُ بِها“ is: one drives away with it and pushes back with it. When Solomon died, he died leaning on it — on his staff — and the jinn did not know of his death until the woodworm (al-araḍa) ate the staff and he fell down. ﴿فَلَمّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الجِنُّ﴾ his death, ﴿أنْ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الغَيْبَ ما لَبِثُوا في العَذابِ المُهِينِ﴾: the meaning is: "because had they known what was hidden from them, they would not have worked in subjection"; they only worked thinking that he was alive, overseeing their work. Some said: mankind perceived [the truth about] the jinn, that if they had known the unseen. It may also be that ”تَبَيَّنَتِ الجِنُّ أنْ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الغَيْبَ“ means that the jinn perceived that they do not know the unseen; they used to give the impression that they knew the unseen, and they perceived that it had become clear to people that they do not know — just as you say to someone who claims something false before you, when you have made it clear to him: "I have shown that what he says is false", although he has always known that; but you wanted to rebuke him and let him know that you have learned the falseness of his claim.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ في مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ﴾: it is also read: ”مَسْكِنِهِمْ“ — “with fatḥa and with kasra on the kāf —, and it is read: “ مَساكِنِهِمْ ”. It is also read: “ لِسَبَأ ” with fatḥa and without declension (tark al-ṣarf), and “ لِسَبَإٍ ”. Whoever reads fatḥa and leaves it undeclined does so because he makes “ سَبَأ ” the name of a tribe; and whoever declines it, with kasra and nunation, makes “ سَبَإٍ ” the name of the man and the name of the clan. All of it is permissible and good. ﴿آيَةٌ جَنَّتانِ﴾: “ آيَةٌ ” is nominative, the noun (ism) of “ كانَ ”; and “ جَنَّتانِ ” is nominative in two ways: as a badal (substitute) for “ آيَةٌ ”, and by an implied [subject], as though, when “ a sign ” was said, it was said: “ the sign is two gardens ”. “ اَلْجَنَّتانِ ” are the two orchards: they had two orchards, an orchard on the right and an orchard on the left. ﴿كُلُوا مِن رِزْقِ رَبِّكم واشْكُرُوا لَهُ﴾: the meaning is: “ it was said to them: eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him ”.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾ is on the meaning: “ this is a good land ”; ﴿وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ is on the meaning: “ and Allah is a forgiving Lord ".

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿فَأعْرَضُوا﴾: the meaning is: they turned away from the command of Allah. ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ العَرِمِ﴾: about ”اَلْعَرِمُ“ there are several views. Abū ʿUbayda said: “ [it is the] plural of “ عَرِمَةٌ ”, which is the dam and the embankment. It is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” is the name of the valley. It is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” here is the name of the rat that bored through the dam on them, which is what is called “ اَلْخُلْدُ ” (the mole-rat). And it is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” is heavy rain. They were living in prosperity, and they had gardens on the right and on the left. A woman would go out with a basket on her head, working with her hands, and walk among those trees, and whatever she needed of the fruit of those trees would fall into her basket. But they were not grateful, so Allah sent a rat against them. They had a dam with gates in it, which they would open for whatever water they needed; that rat bored through it until it was breached upon them, and it flooded those two gardens. ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ﴾, that is: in place of these two gardens that were described, ﴿جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾. And “ أُكْلٍ خَمْطٍ ”: ḍamma and sukūn on the kāf are both permissible; it is read: “ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ ” and “ ذَواتَيْ أُكْلٍ خَمْطٍ ”. The meaning of “ خَمْطٍ ”: every plant that has taken on a bitter taste so that it cannot be eaten is called “ خَمْطٌ ”. In the book of al-Khalīl: “ اَلْخَمْطُ ” is the arāk tree. It has come in the exegesis that “ اَلْخَمْطُ ” is the arāk, and “ أُكُلُهُ " is its fruit; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 25]

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْناهم بِما كَفَرُوا﴾: ”ذَلِكَ“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: "We recompensed them with that for their disbelief". ﴿وَهَلْ نُجازِي إلا الكَفُورَ﴾: it is also read: ”وَهَلْ يُجازى“, and ”وَهَلْ يُجازِي إلّا الكَفُورَ“ is permissible. This is among the things that are asked about; it is said: " Allah, Mighty and Majestic, recompenses the ungrateful and the one who is not ungrateful. The meaning in this verse is that the believer has his evil deeds expiated, while the disbeliever has his deeds nullified and so is recompensed for every evil he does. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1], and He said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 28]. So He, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He nullifies the deeds of the disbeliever, and He informed us that good deeds remove evil deeds, and that the believer's good deeds expiate his evil deeds.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ القُرى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرًى ظاهِرَةً﴾: this is conjoined to His words: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ في مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ جَنَّتانِ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 15] ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ القُرى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرًى ظاهِرَةً﴾. So they had no need of provisions from the valley of Sabaʾ to Syria. It is said: the towns that We blessed are Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and it is also said: Syria. So the towns from the valley of Sabaʾ to all these places were continuous.
﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيها السَّيْرَ﴾: We made their travel by measured stages; wherever they wanted to stay, they alighted at a town in safety.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿فَقالُوا رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا﴾: it is also read: ”رَبَّنا بَعِّدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; it is read: ”رَبُّنا بَعَّدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; it is read: ”رَبَّنا“ in the accusative, ”بَعُدَ بَيْنُ أسْفارِنا“ with ”بَيْنَ“ in the nominative; it is read: ”بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; and it is read: ”رَبُّنا باعَدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“. ﴿وَظَلَمُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾. Whoever reads: ”بَعُدَ بَيْنُ أسْفارِنا“ with ”بَيْنَ“ in the nominative, the meaning is: "what connects with our journeying has become distant". Whoever reads: ”بَعُدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“, the meaning is: "what is between our journeys has become distant", and "our travel between our journeys has become long". Whoever reads: ”باعِدْ“, it is by way of request, and the meaning is that they grew weary of ease and were ungrateful for the blessing, as the people of Moses said: ﴿فادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنا مِمّا تُنْبِتُ الأرْضُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 61], up to His words: ﴿الَّذِي هو أدْنى بِالَّذِي هو خَيْرٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 61]. ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهم كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾, that is: "We scattered them throughout the lands", because when Allah took away their two gardens and flooded their place, they dispersed throughout the lands, and the Arabs came to use them as a proverb for dispersal, saying: ”تَفَرَّقُوا أيْدِيَ سَبَإٍ“ and ”أيادِي سَبَإٍ“ (they scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ). The poet said:
مِن صادِرٍ أوْ وارِدٍ أيْدِي سَبا
(Of those departing or arriving, [scattered like] the hands of Sabaʾ.)
And Kuthayyir said:
أيادِي سَبا يا عَزُّ ما كُنْتُ بَعْدَكم ∗∗∗ فَلَمْ يَحْلُ لِلْعَيْنَيْنِ بِعْدَكِ مَنظَرُ
(Scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ, O ʿAzza, I have been since you [left]; no sight has been sweet to the eyes after you.)

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: it is also read: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ“, with ”إبْلِيسُ“ in the nominative and the ẓann in the accusative. His being true in his supposition is that he supposed of them that, when he led them astray, they would follow him, and he found them so; he said: ﴿فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لأُغْوِيَنَّهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 82] ﴿إلا عِبادَكَ مِنهُمُ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 83]. Whoever says ”صَدَّقَ“ makes the ẓann accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and whoever lightens it, saying ”صَدَقَ“, makes the ẓann accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), on the meaning: "Iblīs was true about them in a supposition he supposed", and "he was true in his supposition". There are two other ways in it. One of them: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنُّهُ“, ”ظَنُّهُ“ being a badal (substitute) for ”إبْلِيسُ“, as the Exalted said: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ قِتالٍ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 217]. And it is permissible: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنُّهُ“ «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, identical to the previous form; the meaning given suggests the reading ṣadaqa … ẓannu Iblīsa]», on the meaning: "the supposition of Iblīs proved true by their following him". Both have been read.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن سُلْطانٍ﴾, that is: he had no proof (ḥujja) over them, as He said: ﴿إنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 65]. ﴿إلا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِالآخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هو مِنها في شَكٍّ﴾, that is: except that We might know that with the knowledge of its occurring from them, and that is what they are recompensed for. Allah knows the unseen, and He knows who will believe from who will disbelieve before the believer believes and the disbeliever disbelieves; but that does not entail reward or punishment. They are rewarded and punished only for what they used to do.
His words: ﴿وَما لَهُ مِنهم مِن ظَهِيرٍ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 22]: He means that those whom they claim to be partners of Allah, of the angels and others, have no partnership, and there is no helper for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in what He created.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إلا لِمَن أذِنَ لَهُ﴾, with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the hamza. The meaning is: ”لِمَن أذِنَ لَهُ“, that is: "for the one whom Allah permits to intercede". It is also permissible [as]: "except for the one for whom He permits intercession to be made", so that ”مَن“ refers to the interceders, or it may refer to those interceded for. The better is that it refers to the interceders, because of His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, since those from whose hearts fear is removed here are the angels. It is also read: ”حَتّى إذا فَزَّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“ with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and al-Ḥasan read: ”حَتّى إذا فُرِّغَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“, with the undotted rāʾ and the dotted ghayn. The meaning of ”فُزِّعَ“ is: fear was removed from their hearts; and ”فَزَّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“: Allah removed fear from their hearts. Al-Ḥasan's reading ”فُرِّغَ“ comes back to this meaning, because they were emptied of fear. The explanation of this is that when Gabriel — upon him be peace — descended to Muḥammad ﷺ with revelation, the angels thought that he had descended for something of the matter of the Hour, and they were terrified at that. When the fear was removed from them, ﴿قالُوا ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾, asking: "For what is Gabriel descending?" ﴿قالُوا الحَقَّ﴾, that is: they said: He said the truth. Had it been read: ”قالُوا الحَقُّ“, it would be a valid way, the meaning being: "they said: it is the truth".

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿وَإنّا أوْ إيّاكم لَعَلى هُدًى أوْ في ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: it is related in the exegesis that the meaning is: "We are surely upon guidance, and you are surely in manifest error". This is not permissible in the language, but in exegesis it comes back to this meaning: "We are upon guidance or in manifest error, or you are upon guidance or in manifest error". This is like when someone says — when the situation indicates that he is truthful —: "One of us is truthful and one of us is a liar", the meaning being: "one of us is truthful or a liar". The meaning of the verse comes back to: "We, because of the proof we have established, are upon guidance, and you are in manifest error".

zajjaj:26-26.t: His words: ﴿ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنا بِالحَقِّ﴾: the meaning of ”يَفْتَحُ“ is: He judges; and likewise ”اَلْفَتّاحُ“ is the Judge.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ أرُونِيَ الَّذِينَ ألْحَقْتُمْ بِهِ شُرَكاءَ﴾: the meaning is: ”ألْحَقْتُمُوهم بِهِ“ (you joined them to Him), but [the pronoun] was omitted because it is in the ṣila (relative clause) of ”اَلَّذِينَ“.
His words: ﴿كَلا بَلْ هو اللَّهُ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾: the meaning of ”كَلّا“ is deterrence and alerting; the meaning is: "Desist from this saying and wake up from your misguidance; rather, He is Allah, the One, like whom there is nothing."

zajjaj:28-28.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا كافَّةً لِلنّاسِ بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾: the meaning of ”كافَّةً“ in the language is encompassing; the meaning is: “We sent you encompassing all people in warning and conveying. So Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ to the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and he said: «“ I am the forerunner of the Arabs to Islam, Ṣuhayb is the forerunner of the Byzantines, Bilāl is the forerunner of the Abyssinians, and Salmān is the forerunner of the Persians "», that is: the message is universal, and these are the forerunners from among the non-Arabs.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His words: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ بِهَذا القُرْآنِ ولا بِالَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: they mean: "We do not believe in what Muḥammad ﷺ has brought, nor in the earlier scriptures."

zajjaj:33-33.t: His words: ﴿بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾: its meaning is: "rather, your scheming by night and day". ﴿وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُ أنْدادًا﴾: likenesses. ﴿وَأسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمّا رَأوُا العَذابَ﴾: “they concealed it among themselves; they turned to blaming one another and making one another aware of the remorse. ﴿إلا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها﴾ [Sabaʾ: 34]: “ مُتْرَفُوها " are those of luxury, and they are its chiefs and the leaders of evil, whom the lowly follow.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أمْوالُكم ولا أوْلادُكم بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكم عِنْدَنا زُلْفى﴾: He did not say ”بِاللَّتَيْنِ“, nor ”بِاللَّذَيْنِ“, nor ”بِاللّاتِي“, and all of that would be permissible, but what is in the Muṣḥaf is ”اَلَّتِي“. The meaning is: "Your wealth is not that which brings you near, nor are your children those who bring you near", but [one of the two] was omitted for brevity and concision; we have explained the like of this.
His words: ﴿إلا مَن آمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is accusative by exception, as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm, on the meaning: “nothing brings near except [for] whoever believes and does righteous deeds", that is: “ wealth brings near only whoever believes and uses it in obedience to Allah ”. ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا﴾: “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” here needs explanation, and I know of no one who has explained it clearly. “ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ ” here is ten good deeds; its interpretation is: “ for those there is the recompense of the multiple whose measure We have made known to you ”, and that is His words: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 160]. There are several ways in it in Arabic. What has been read is the genitive of “ اَلضِّعْفِ ”, by annexing the recompense to it. It is permissible: “ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءٌ الضِّعْفُ ”, on the meaning: “ for those there is the multiple as a recompense ”, the meaning being: “ in the state of recompensing ”. It is permissible: “ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءً الضِّعْفَ ”, with “ اَلضِّعْفَ ” in the accusative, the meaning being: “ for those it is that We recompense them the multiple ”. The nominative of “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” is permissible on two accounts: on the meaning: “ for those there is the multiple ”, “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” being a badal (substitute) for the recompense; and it may be nominative with “ هو ” implied: “ for those there is a recompense ” — as though one asked: What is it? And He said: “ the multiple ”. The accusative in “ اَلضِّعْفِ ” is also permissible as the object of a verb whose agent is not named (i.e. passive), on the meaning: “ for those it is that they be recompensed the multiple ”. The reading, of all these ways, is the genitive of “ اَلضِّعْفِ ” and the nominative of “ جَزاءٌ ".

zajjaj:44-44.t: His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما آتَيْناهم مِن كُتُبٍ يَدْرُسُونَها وما أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِن نَذِيرٍ﴾: by this are meant the Arab idolaters in Mecca; they were not people of scriptures, and no prophet was sent [to them] before Muḥammad ﷺ.

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وما بَلَغُوا مِعْشارَ ما آتَيْناهُمْ﴾, that is: a tenth of the strength and power that We gave those before them. ﴿فَكَذَّبُوا رُسُلِي فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ﴾: the yāʾ was dropped; the meaning is: "So how was My reproach (nakīrī)?", because it is the end of a verse.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما أعِظُكم بِواحِدَةٍ﴾, that is: I exhort you to affirm the oneness of Allah and to say: "There is no god but Allah", sincerely. It is also said: ”واحِدَةٍ“ concerns obedience, and obedience includes affirming oneness and sincerity; the meaning is: "I exhort you with this one trait". ﴿أنْ تَقُومُوا﴾, that is: "that you may stand"; ﴿أنْ تَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ مَثْنى وفُرادى﴾, that is: I exhort you to obedience to Allah, that you may stand for Allah singly and together. ﴿ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا ما بِصاحِبِكم مِن جِنَّةٍ﴾: the meaning is: "then reflect, and you will know that the Prophet ﷺ is not mad, as you say". ”اَلْجِنَّةُ“ is madness. ﴿إنْ هو إلا نَذِيرٌ لَكم بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾, that is: he warns you that if you disobey you will meet a severe punishment.

zajjaj:47-47.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ ما سَألْتُكم مِن أجْرٍ فَهو لَكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: "Whatever wage I have asked of you for the message I convey to you and the Quran I have brought you from Allah, it is yours." Its interpretation is: I only warn you and convey the message to you, and I am not drawing to myself any of the goods of this world. ﴿إنْ أجْرِيَ إلا عَلى اللَّهِ﴾, that is: I seek only the reward of Allah by conveying the message. The yāʾ in ”أجْرِي“ is [read] quiescent and with fatḥa, and the better is the fatḥa, because it is a noun (ism) and so is made indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالحَقِّ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾ — and with kasra on the ghayn —; ”عَلّامَ الغُيُوبِ“ in the accusative is also permissible. Whoever reads the accusative, ”عَلّامَ الغُيُوبِ“ is an attribute (ṣifa) of ”رَبِّي“; the meaning is: "Say: my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, hurls the truth". Whoever reads ”عَلّامُ الغُيُوبِ“ in the nominative, it is on two accounts. One of them is that it be an attribute on the position of ”إنَّ رَبِّي“, because its interpretation is: "Say: my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, hurls the truth", ”إنَّ“ being emphatic.
And the nominative is permissible as a badal (substitute) for what is in ”يَقْذِفُ“ [i.e. its pronoun]; the meaning is: "Say: my Lord hurls — He, the Knower of the unseen — the truth". The meaning of ”يَقْذِفُ بِالحَقِّ“ is: "He brings the truth" and "He casts the truth", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالحَقِّ عَلى الباطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 18]

zajjaj:49-49.t: His words: ﴿قُلْ جاءَ الحَقُّ وما يُبْدِئُ الباطِلُ وما يُعِيدُ﴾, that is: "Say: the command of Allah, which is the truth, has come; and what does falsehood originate?" ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative, on the meaning: "And what thing does falsehood originate? And what thing does it bring back?" The better is that ”ما“ be negative, on the meaning: "falsehood neither originates nor brings back". ”اَلْباطِلُ“ here is Iblīs; the meaning is: "Iblīs neither brings back nor benefits" «[Translator's note: so in the source (”وَما يُعِيدُ إبْلِيسُ وما يُفِيدُ“); one would expect "neither originates nor brings back"]», that is: "he neither creates nor resurrects, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Creator and the Resurrector". It may also be that ”اَلْباطِلُ“ is the one of falsehood, who is Iblīs.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إذْ فَزِعُوا فَلا فَوْتَ﴾.
His words: ﴿فَلا فَوْتَ﴾, that is: there is no escape for them; they cannot get away. ﴿وَأُخِذُوا مِن مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾: in the exegesis: from beneath their feet. ”فَلا فَوْتٌ“ is also permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; if no transmission is established for it, do not read it, for reading [the Quran] is a sunna (an established practice).

zajjaj:52-52.t: His words: ﴿وَقالُوا آمَنّا بِهِ وأنّى لَهُمُ التَّناوُشُ مِن مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾: they said "We believe" at the time about which Allah, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿لا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إيمانُها لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 158]. ”اَلتَّناوُشُ“ is reaching for something, that is: how could they reach what was offered freely to them and was near them?! How then can they reach it when it has become far from them?! Whoever uses hamza, saying ”اَلتَّناؤُشُ“, does so because the wāw of ”اَلتَّناؤُشُ“ has ḍamma, and with every wāw whose ḍamma is permanent, you may, if you wish, replace it with a hamza, or, if you wish, not replace it — as when you say ”أدْوُرٌ“ and ”تَقاوُمٌ“, or, if you wish, say ”أدْؤُرٌ“ and ”تَقاؤُمٌ“ with hamza. It may also be that ”اَلتَّناؤُشُ“ is from ”اَلنَّئِيشُ“, which is moving slowly; so the meaning is: "How could they move in a matter in which they have no recourse?!"

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِهِ مِن قَبْلُ ويَقْذِفُونَ بِالغَيْبِ مِن مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, that is: they used to make guesses and cast at the unseen; and their guessing was that they supposed they would not be resurrected.

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ ما يَشْتَهُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "of returning to the world, and faith". ﴿كَما فُعِلَ بِأشْياعِهِمْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: with those whose way was their way. ﴿إنَّهم كانُوا في شَكٍّ مُرِيبٍ﴾: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has informed us that He punishes for doubt. Some of the misguided have said that the doubters bear no liability; this is disbelief and a contradiction of the Quran, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَما خَلَقْنا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما باطِلا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 27]
